title: I Followed the Malicious Compliance Through Three Layers of Badge Policy

parts.text: I badged in and the system called me a visitor in my own building. I am thirty-one, night supervisor, Folgers burnt, again. Vince had locked regular badges to day shift to 'reduce overtime leakage.' Night crew got visitor stickers that peeled in the cold. The sticker glue smelled like bananas. Marisol's sticker fell onto a pallet jack. I emailed HR a photo. Vince said work around it. Vince said, "Nights can use the side door" I said, "The side door needs a real badge" The visitor door closed at 10 p.m. sharp, a new rule. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The visitor door is locked, our stickers peel, and the side door wants the badges he disabled.

parts.text: I lined up twenty visitor stickers on the glass for the morning cameras. I did not break in. I clocked a safety stop because a crew without badges cannot enter a secured floor, per Vince's own memo from January. The line stopped. Packages sat. Vince called my personal phone, cinnamon-less, just spit. I forwarded the January memo. Facilities arrived, annoyed, professional. They issued temp real badges, paper but magnetic. Marisol almost cried, then laughed. Vince accused me of a stunt. The stunt was literacy. Facilities said, "Who disabled night credentials" Vince said, "It was a pilot" The banana smell faded as stickers died in the trash. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. parts.cliffhanger_hint: Temp badges are in our pockets, packages are late, and Vince is calling it a pilot on a recorded facilities line.

parts.text: I sat in the 9 a.m. meeting with the January memo printed. Gwen from payroll was there because late packages cost money, the language they hear. Vince tried family again. I tried timestamps. Night credentials came back that afternoon. Visitor stickers returned to actual visitors. I did not get a parade. I got my mug. The pallet jack still squeaks. Marisol bought real coffee once, dangerous, delicious. Vince transferred to a site with more daylight, which is poetry. I still check the side door on habit. Habit is how policies fail, and how they get caught. Gwen said, "What did the pilot save" Vince said, "I'll get back to you" HR asked if I wanted a statement. I said the memo was the statement.
